conventions.convention: Biological replicates are distinct biological units; technical replicates are repeated readings or assays of the same specimen. Neither label asserts independence.
Responses and data-dependent predictors are specified measurable maps into named measurable target spaces.

Latent quantities must separately be declared fixed or random. Indexing, unit labels, and adequacy classifications imply no independence, exchangeability, missingness, causal identification, or common support.
An asserted support set is measurable and has probability one; topological support requires a separately named topology and conditions.
A stochastic observation mechanism has probability-measure sections and measurable state dependence. Conditioning at a zero-probability event requires a specified version and existence hypotheses.

The eight-participant example averages over uniform assignment of exactly four treated participants among 70 assignments. Outcomes and reading offsets are fixed; both assignment and all 48 response coordinates are observed.
The calibration example has unrestricted parameter set R², power-set observation sigma-algebra, law δ(q+b), and target ψ(q,b)=q.

load_bearing.statement: A scientific statistical model contract is an explicit record for a specified analysis of observation space and record; scientific, sampling, assignment, and analysis units; indices and time; quantity status; target and estimand; observation mechanism; support and law; conditioning convention; and adequacy assumptions. These are bookkeeping and interpretation requirements and establish no empirical applicability.

For sample space (R, P(R)), parameter set Θ=R², sampling law P(q,b)=δ(q+b), and target ψ(q,b)=q, the target is not identifiable: (q,b) and (q+1,b−1) have identical sampling laws and different target values.

published_dependencies.used_for: The measurable observation space and parameter-indexed family of probability laws in the contract and both examples.
The parameter-to-law map, without an injectivity or parameter-measurability assumption.
The specified target-valued function on the parameter set in the contract and examples.
Equality of sampling laws in the identifiability prerequisite.
Equal sampling laws must imply equal target values; the calibration example violates this implication.
The measurable-map convention for recorded responses and predictors.
Measurable random quantities, record maps, and coordinate extractors.
The pushforward definition of the recorded-data law.
Power-set observation and assignment measurable spaces in the repeated-visits construction.
Countable additivity of the finite uniform assignment measure.
Total mass one and the probability-space interpretation.
Measurability of record maps and extractors by their preimages.
The pushforward record law in the repeated-visits example is a probability measure.
The calibration law assigns mass one exactly to sets containing q+b.
Each calibration sampling law is a probability measure on the chosen power-set sigma-algebra.

alerts.finding: The Definition says: “A biological replicate is another independently sampled unit at that same level under the sampling law being modeled.” It subsequently says that replicate names “do not assert statistical independence.” The cited def-scientific-statistical-model-contract, field 2, instead defines a biological replicate as “a distinct biological unit” and explicitly says “Neither term asserts independence.” Thus the opening terminology incorporates independence into the replicate label, conflicting with both its cited convention and its own later disclaimer. The particular random-intercept model separately states mutual independence, so this finding concerns the terminology rather than that model's variance assumptions.

seams_checked.note: The page and regression definition explicitly distinguish abstract model-side fields from a complete application contract. Fixed X supplies no sampling or assignment law or adequacy conclusion.
The page requires a separate scientific application contract. The observation-family definition states independence and common support explicitly rather than deriving them from the contract.
The sample-model definition records vector units, indices, fixed parameters, observed random vectors, identity observation, and the joint product law, while disclaiming physical applicability.
The PCA definition invokes the contract only to distinguish mathematical matrices under an assumed law from evidence of empirical adequacy.

The mixed-model definition keeps subject and visit roles distinct. The missingness definition supplies a finite-output measurable probability kernel and does not infer ignorability from covariance equations.
The sampling-design definition holds population values fixed, randomizes sampled subsets, and requires the finite-population target and sampling unit to be recorded separately.

The assignment-model definition records fixed schedules, random assignments, the observed record, support, and averaging convention. Its adequacy classifications distinguish positive-probability assignments from unobservable zero-probability assignments.

The page correctly requires explicit independence assumptions, but its model definition calls a biological replicate an independently sampled unit, conflicting with the supplier's independence-free label convention. Exact evidence is in alerts.

The likelihood theorem records subject units, the censoring observation map, conditioning on observed covariates, and no empirical adequacy claim. Conditional identities are qualified almost everywhere for each parameter pair.
The measurement definition faithfully restates the contract fields and separates uncertainty calculations from evidence that a measurement model applies physically.

This is contextual compatibility rather than an explicit contract citation: the page and definition declare measurement conditions and target population, require repeated-measurement dependence to be modeled, and infer neither calibration nor scientific acceptability.

The page expressly limits its contract discussion to observation, index, quantity-status, and law fields; physical units and population remain application fields. Stationarity and global asymptotic hypotheses are not certified by a finite record.

The page distinguishes random latent paths from observed projections and leaves scientific units and target population application-specific. The kernel definition invokes the contract without asserting empirical adequacy.
